defects.what: `disabled={!markdown.data?.markdown}` can never be true: the button only renders inside the `markdown.data ?` branch. The optional chaining is dead too. The report says so openly and keeps the prop to follow the brief's wording, so this is a harmless nit.

structured_output.summary:
The change adds a "Download .md" button beside the deck guide's copy button. Its `download()` copies the RCQ `CarryCard` pattern exactly: a Blob, an anchor named `deck-guide.md`, and a revoke after 1 s. The button is `variant="secondary"`, matches the copy button's `size="sm"`, and sits with it in one wrapper div; the old `mb-2` moved onto that div. The new key `decks.guide.export.download` has the exact wording the brief asked for in en and pt-BR. Only the three allowed files changed. All checks pass (lint, test, tsc, pytest).

The reference pulls the download into a shared `lib/download.ts` and also edits docs. Neither was possible within this brief's file list, so the inline duplicate is the correct call here, not a defect.

The report's choice of an undated file name holds up. The only date in scope is `response?.authored_at`, which dates the narrative and is null when there is none, so the brief's rule leads to plain `deck-guide.md`. The report matches the diff and says the browser save was not verified.

The only nit is the redundant `disabled` guard, which the report already points out. The brief needed no new test, and existing coverage still holds.
